pharm: Anticholinergic that blocks responses of the iris sphincter and ciliary accommodative muscle to cholinergic stimulation, producing mydriasis and cycloplegia.
quick: 1-2 drops of 0.5%, 1%, or 2% in the eye; may repeat in 5-10 minutes
Not applicable (ophthalmic); withhold infant feeding 4 hours after exam
Use only if clearly needed; animal data lacking
Excretion in milk unknown; use with caution
IOP; CNS/cardiopulmonary effects in children/infants; observe infants 30 min
summary: Cyclopentolate hydrochloride (Cyclogyl) is an ophthalmic anticholinergic used to produce mydriasis and cycloplegia for diagnostic purposes. It acts rapidly with a shorter duration than atropine. It may cause CNS disturbances, especially in younger patients and with stronger (2%) solutions, and infants are especially prone to CNS and cardiopulmonary effects. Nasolacrimal pressure for 2-3 minutes reduces systemic absorption. In infants, feeding intolerance and rare cases of necrotizing enterocolitis have been reported; withhold feeding for 4 hours after the examination.

dosage.t: May repeat in 5-10 minutes if necessary
dosage.n: Recovery usually within 24 hours; mydriasis may take several days to fully resolve in some individuals

dosage.d: 1 or 2 drops of 0.5%, 1%, or 2% solution; may follow in 5-10 minutes with a second application of 0.5% or 1%
dosage.n: Heavily pigmented irides may need higher strengths
Apply nasolacrimal sac pressure 2-3 minutes to minimize absorption; observe at least 30 minutes; withhold feeding 4 hours after exam

admin: For topical ophthalmic use only; NOT for injection
Compress the lacrimal sac by digital pressure for 2-3 minutes after instillation to reduce systemic absorption
In infants use only 1 drop of 0.5%, apply nasolacrimal pressure, and observe closely for at least 30 minutes
Do not touch the dropper tip to any surface to avoid contamination
Wash the patient's and the caregiver's hands after administration; do not let preparation reach a child's mouth
moa: Cyclopentolate is an anticholinergic that blocks the muscarinic responses of the iris sphincter muscle and the ciliary body accommodative muscle, producing pupillary dilation (mydriasis) and paralysis of accommodation (cycloplegia). Maximal cycloplegia occurs within 25-75 minutes; it acts rapidly but with a shorter duration than atropine.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to any component of the preparation
relative: Untreated narrow-angle glaucoma or anatomically narrow angles (risk of angle closure)
Infants and young children, and children with spastic paralysis or brain damage (increased susceptibility to CNS effects)
monitor: CNS and cardiopulmonary effects in children and infants

preg: Animal reproduction studies have not been conducted with cyclopentolate. It is not known whether it can cause fetal harm or affect reproductive capacity. Administer to a pregnant woman only if clearly needed.
lact: It is not known whether cyclopentolate is excreted in human milk. Because many drugs are excreted in human milk, exercise caution when administering to a nursing woman.
renal: No dosage adjustment described; systemic absorption is minimal with proper technique (nasolacrimal occlusion).
hepatic: No dosage adjustment described; systemic absorption is minimal with proper technique.

moderate: Carbachol, pilocarpine, or ophthalmic cholinesterase inhibitors: cyclopentolate may interfere with their ocular antihypertensive (IOP-lowering) action
interactions.food: Not applicable (ophthalmic); withhold infant feeding for 4 hours after the examination.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction noted in labeling.
interactions.diagnostics: Used as a diagnostic agent for cycloplegic refraction and fundus examination; transiently elevates intraocular pressure.

serious: Increased intraocular pressure / angle-closure in susceptible eyes
Psychotic reactions and behavioral disturbances (especially children, 2% solution)
rare: Necrotizing enterocolitis and feeding intolerance in preterm infants

monitoring: Intraocular pressure, particularly in patients with narrow angles or glaucoma
CNS and cardiopulmonary status in children and infants (observe at least 30 minutes)
Feeding tolerance in infants after the procedure
counsel: A transient burning sensation may occur on instillation
Do not drive or perform hazardous activities while the pupils are dilated
You may be sensitive to light; protect your eyes in bright light during dilation
Parents: keep the preparation out of the child's mouth and wash both your and the child's hands after use
In infants, feeding may be withheld for 4 hours after the examination
pk: Cycloplegic effect peaks 25-75 minutes after instillation
Recovery of accommodation usually 6-24 hours; mydriasis may take several days to fully resolve
Store at 8-25 C (46-77 F); usable until expiration date after opening
pearls: Shorter duration of action than atropine, making it convenient for diagnostic cycloplegic refraction
Nasolacrimal sac pressure for 2-3 minutes substantially reduces systemic anticholinergic absorption
Use the lowest effective strength in infants and young children to limit CNS and cardiopulmonary effects
Heavily pigmented irides may require higher strengths or more doses
missed: Not applicable; cyclopentolate is administered as a single diagnostic dose (or brief repeat instillations) by a clinician rather than on a maintenance schedule.
overdose: Excessive dosage may produce behavioral disturbances, tachycardia, hyperpyrexia, hypertension, elevated intraocular pressure, vasodilation, urinary retention, diminished GI motility, and decreased salivary/sweat/respiratory secretions; severe toxicity can include coma, medullary paralysis, and death. Provide supportive care and monitoring; physostigmine may be considered for severe central anticholinergic toxicity per standard care.
